newsitem.title: USA: Venezuela to hold bids for more old oil fields.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to hold bids for more old oil fields.

text.p: State oil company Petroleos de Venezuela SA may set plans next month for a new oil bidding round to attract foreign companies to revitalize up to as many as 20 old fields, a top PDVSA executive said Wednesday.

"We plan to have a third round of (bidding for) operational contracts that will be announced in October of this year," Juan Szabo, head of PDVSA's exploration and production told executives at the AIC Latin Oil Conference here.

Szabo later told Reuters PDVSA will likely put up between 12 and 20 fields for bidding in the round, which could take place some time during 1997. Szabo did not elaborate on which fields might be included in the bidding.

"We want to make sure the bidding is just as exciting as the exploration round," Szabo said, referring to the often-dramatic bidding bidding in January in Caracas for exploration rights on 10 tracts in Venezuela.
Eight of those 10 tracts were contracted out, but Szabo said one of the two fields not auctioned in January may go back on the bidding block before the end of the year.

Executives at the Latin Oil conference said they hoped terms of the bidding on that field, called Catatumbo and located on the southwestern shores of Venezuela's oil-rich Lake Maracaibo, would be more favorable to bidders than originally conceived.
That exploration round marked the first time Venezuela had opened up its vast oil acreage to foreigners since the industry was nationalized 20 years ago.

Bringing foreign companies into Venezuela for revitalization or exploration of old or new oil fields is a key part of the country's strategy to dramatically expand its crude oil production to about 6.3 million barrels per day (bpd) between now and 2006.

Industry sources said Venezuela is already producing well above its OPEC output quota of around 2.359 million bpd, but Szabo and other PDVSA executives attending the conference all declined to discuss Venezuela's alleged quota infractions.
